issue.title: Mac CaptureRelatedLaneTests rapid-edit debounce test records two capture-related calls under CI load
issue.description:
Observed by the bob-cli-hl.5.1 lander on bob-mac-capture tree 922561578967e4120c4d6ac5467a2d09dbe33b7d (identical tree on two SHAs):

- FAIL: master a3e533b9ec57855be534ac4d96b8bcd7cb8194bf, macOS CI run 42216904060 (2026-11-06T12:20Z):
  `CaptureRelatedLaneTests.swift:88` and `:94`: `XCTAssertEqual failed: ("2") is not equal to ("1")` — two `capture-related` calls were recorded where the test expects one.
- PASS: CI snapshot 04041733ce1334db799fa3cdf93c7c94eba8a1da (same tree), run 42212293089.
- PASS: pre-epic master 6f4e279 run 42161345004 and 9578c66 run 42209303483.

Fail rate observed: 1 of 4 recent full macOS suite runs; only seen in full parallel `swift test` on the GitHub macOS 26 runner, never reproduced serially (no Mac XCTest available off CI).

Likely root cause: the test uses fixed wall-clock sleeps around a 100 ms Similar-tasks settle window (`typeDraft("Install")`, `Task.sleep(35 ms)`, then the full draft, then `Task.sleep(160 ms)`). If the runner stalls for more than ~65 ms between the two edits, the first draft settles and records an extra `capture-related` call. Fix by driving the settle deterministically (injectable clock/settle hook or a much larger settle interval relative to the gap), not by loosening the count assertion.
